outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain written confirmation from SF Planning that Section 202.12 requires a CUA for this laundromat conversion. What to say: Request a pre-application meeting or zoning letter from the SF Planning Department, citing the September 8, 2022 agency referral denial at 779 Bush St (case 2022-008099MIS) and asking whether a Conditional Use Authorization under Planning Code Section 202.12 is still required for a laundromat-to-bar conversion, and whether any other discretionary approvals apply. Bring the project description, floor plan and photographs of the existing space. Do not file or pay for any other application until you have this answer in writing.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning, including environmental review and neighborhood notification. What to say: Submit the CUA application (Planning Code Section 303) with required materials: project description, floor plans, elevation drawings showing the storefront, menu, proposed hours, security plan, good-neighbor commitments (contact number, complaint response protocol, periodic meetings with neighbors), and any acoustic or operational measures to mitigate noise. The application must explain why the laundromat conversion serves the public necessity and will not be detrimental to nearby properties (Section 303(c) findings). Schedule and conduct the required pre-application community meeting within 300 feet. Expect Planning to route the application for environmental review (likely a categorical exemption) and to post 300-foot mailed notice before the Planning Commission hearing.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Attend Planning Commission hearing and obtain approval of the Conditional Use Authorization. What to say: Present the project at the Commission hearing, emphasizing the quality and design of the bar, the good-neighbor commitments, security and noise-mitigation measures, and the public benefit of activating the vacant laundromat space. Be prepared to accept conditions on hours (closing by midnight or 1 am), sound limits, security staffing, and possibly a restriction to beer-and-wine service if Commissioners express concern about the high alcohol-license density in the area (24 on-sale licenses within 500 ft). If the Commission approves with conditions, the approval becomes final after a 30-day appeal period unless an appeal is filed.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for ABC licence (type to be determined) after the CUA is final and unappealed. What to say: Submit the ABC application (original or transfer, depending on your plan) with the signed lease, approved CUA decision, California seller's permit, entity registration, and proof that the business account is registered with SF Treasurer & Tax Collector. ABC will refer the application to SF Planning and SFPD for review; Planning will approve it based on the CUA. If the census tract is designated undue concentration, request a Public Convenience or Necessity letter from the SF Board of Supervisors or Planning at the same time you apply to ABC, explaining the community benefit and citing the CUA findings. Post the ABC notice at the premises for 30 days and expect 55–65 days for an unprotested beer-and-wine licence, or 90–180 days (plus escrow time) for a transferred spirits licence.
outcomes.note: The records show Planning reviews ABC referrals and undue concentration exists, but do not state the application procedures, required documents, review processes, or timelines described.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File building permit application with tenant-improvement plans, DPH plan check and change-of-use documentation. What to say: Submit the building permit application to SF Department of Building Inspection with architectural plans stamped by a licensed architect, showing the bar layout, kitchen (limited cooking equipment), restrooms, ADA access, exit paths and occupancy calculation. Route the application to DPH for plan check of food-service equipment, finishes and menu. Attach the approved CUA and state that the use has been authorized by the Planning Commission. DBI will refer the permit to Planning per Section 175(a); Planning will confirm that it conforms to the CUA conditions before issuing the permit. Schedule electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits with licensed subcontractors, and coordinate the grease-interceptor installation with SFPUC under the FOG ordinance.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for health permit to operate after DPH plan check is approved and construction is substantially complete. What to say: Submit the health permit application online with the Business Account Number (BAN), Location ID and federal EIN at least one month before the planned opening. Confirm that a certified food safety manager is on staff (ServSafe or equivalent) and that all employees will obtain California food handler cards within 30 days of hire. Schedule the pre-opening inspection with DPH at about 80% construction complete to catch any issues early, then schedule the final inspection for after all equipment, finishes and hot water are in place. The permit is issued after the final inspection passes.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain sign permit for exterior business signage. What to say: Submit sign permit application to SF Planning and DBI with drawings and dimensions of the proposed exterior sign and any illuminated elements. Planning reviews for size and illumination compliance with the RC-4 district rules. If the building is in a historic district or is an Article 10/11 landmark, the review will take longer. File this in parallel with the building permit to avoid delaying the opening.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Complete all business formation, registration, tax and insurance filings before opening. What to say: Form the legal entity (LLC or corporation) with the California Secretary of State; obtain the federal EIN from the IRS online; register for a California seller's permit with CDTFA; register as an employer with EDD; obtain workers' compensation insurance; register the business with SF Treasurer & Tax Collector and file a fictitious business name statement with the County Clerk if the public name differs from the entity name. These are prerequisites for the ABC application, the building permit and the health permit, so complete them early. Also register for RBS training through the ABC portal and ensure every alcohol server and manager completes certification within 60 days of hire. Subscribe to ASCAP and BMI licences for recorded music before opening.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $15,000. Notes: The day and cost ranges are for the Conditional Use Authorization, which is the critical-path approval; they are times and costs to approval when the CUA is granted. The catalog shows 120–300 days and $3,100–$15,000 for a CUA, with higher fees when construction valuation is high. The comparable CUA at 532–536 Sutter (2013.0508C) took 708 days from filing to withdrawal, illustrating the timeline and uncertainty of a discretionary hearing. After the CUA is approved and final, the ABC licence (type not yet determined) adds 60–240 days depending on type and undue-concentration status, the building permit adds 14–120 days, and the health permit adds 14–45 days; these approvals can overlap. Total timeline from CUA filing to opening is likely 10–18 months if the CUA is approved, or longer if appealed or denied. Business registration, entity formation, seller's permit and other administrative filings add minimal time (1–35 days) and $125–1,070 in government fees, and should be completed early.
